explanation.headline: Liquidity is one-sided with no ask, preventing exit of any position.
explanation.summary: The market has one-sided liquidity, with no ask price, and a tiny, fully withdrawable depth. Most of the window has passed (82% elapsed, about 265 min remaining) and there has been no trading, leaving volatility and manipulation unmeasured. Together this means you can open a position but cannot reliably exit it, and price information is largely speculative.

perSignal.reading: You could enter a trade but have no quoted price to exit, making exit uncertain.
The tiny, fully withdrawable depth means the displayed quotes can disappear instantly, offering little guaranteed liquidity.
With no trade history, price volatility cannot be gauged, leaving price movement risk undefined.
The mid price is just an initial estimate and may be far from any later market price.
Time remaining is limited, and most of the market's lifespan has passed, so there is little time for new information to shift prices.
Because there is no trade flow, any potential manipulation cannot be evaluated at this stage.
